newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to up slightly Thursday in thin trade, with firmer crude underpinning the complex but few expecting much upside with gas cheap and spring fast approaching.

"Gas is still cleaning resid's clock on the East Coast. Volume has dried up and I don't see any great demand around the corner," said one cash trader, noting most East Coast utilities have made the switch to gas.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up slightly to the $15.00-25 a barrel, while March and April one percent paper also gained modestly to $15.10-35, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour again was unchanged at $17.00-25, with a slightly off-spec piece of West African material offered at $16.75, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York remained stable.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent gained 25 cents to $13.50 on reports an aggressive seller had raised his offer.

USG three percent gained slightly to about $12 on reports two 45,000-barrel prompt barges sold Wednesday at $12.00 and $12.05 (delivered Houston). USG March three percent paper rose 30 cents with crude to about $12.60, traders said.

New York city gate swing gas prices were steady to up slightly in the $2.20s/mmBtu, or about $14.18 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, slipped almost 10 cents to the low-$1.80s/mmBtu, or $11.47 a barrel equivalent.
